description: Asking a model to read a document and return entities and relations as structured data, usually JSON, to build a knowledge graph.
The ontology's types and relations go into the prompt, so the model uses your vocabulary; a validator rejects whatever falls outside it.
When a reply does not parse, call again with the bad reply and a short correction in the history. Capped, and never used for refusals.
Deciding which mentions refer to the same real-world thing ("Acme Corp." and "ACME Corporation") and merging them, within the same type.
Lowercasing, stripping accents and punctuation, and dropping legal suffixes, so spelling variants share one key.
Comparing only candidates that share a cheap key (first letters, postcode) before expensive fuzzy or semantic matching, to avoid comparing everything with everything.
The sources that asserted each fact (document, chunk, run, model version). Enables citations, audits, deletion and re-extraction.
Every extracted item that failed validation, with its document and reason. A dataset for improving the prompt or the ontology.
